```{r}
library(readr)
library(limma)        # differential testing (empirical Bayes)
library(ggplot2)      # plotting
library(qqman)        # quick QQ and Manhattan plots (genomics style)
library(qqplotr)      # ggplot2-friendly QQ plots
library(mixOmics)     # DIABLO and other multi-omics methods
library(glmnet)       # Lasso / elastic net
library(data.table)   # fast I/O and data handling
```


```{r}

# Read the table
mtb <- read_tsv("mtb.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# 1. Save the first column as a vector
first_col <- mtb[[1]]

# 2. Set it as rownames
mtb <- as.data.frame(mtb)   # ensure it's a data frame
rownames(mtb) <- first_col

# 3. Remove the first column from the data
mtb <- mtb[ , -1, drop = FALSE]


metadata <- read_tsv(
  "metadata.tsv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Read the table
Meg <- read_tsv("genera.counts.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Convert tibble → data frame (tibbles do not support rownames)
Meg <- as.data.frame(Meg)

# Save the first column as rownames
rownames(Meg) <- Meg[[1]]

# Remove the first column
Meg <- Meg[ , -1, drop = FALSE]

metadata$Sample
```
## Data Pre processing 

```{r}
# 1. Extract clean sample IDs from metadata
ids <- metadata$Sample

# 2. Extract rownames from mtb and Meg
ids_mtb <- rownames(mtb)
ids_meg <- rownames(Meg)

# 3. Check which metadata IDs are missing in mtb and Meg
setdiff(ids, ids_mtb)
setdiff(ids, ids_meg)

# 4. Check which mtb or Meg IDs are not in metadata
setdiff(ids_mtb, ids)
setdiff(ids_meg, ids)

# 5. Quick TRUE/FALSE check for perfect matching
all(ids %in% ids_mtb)
all(ids %in% ids_meg)

```

## Check for the covarates to be sure before doing the diff analysis 
```{r}
library(mixOmics)

# Match samples
mtb_DA <- mtb[rownames(mtb) %in% metadata$Sample, , drop = FALSE]
# mtb_DA: samples x metabolites

group <- metadata$Study.Group[match(rownames(mtb_DA), metadata$Sample)]
group <- factor(group)

mtb_scaled <- scale(mtb_DA, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
# PCA on all samples together
pca.mtb <- pca(mtb_scaled, ncomp = 5, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)

my_cols <- c("#1b9e77", "#d95f02","#7570b3")

plotIndiv(
  pca.mtb,
  group     = group,
  ind.names = FALSE,
  ellipse   = TRUE,
  legend    = TRUE,
  pch       = 1,
  cex       = 1.4,
  col       = my_cols
)

table(group)
plotVar(pca.mtb, var.names = FALSE, title = "Metabolite loadings")


```
## test for covarattes 

```{r}

# 1. Ensure rownames of mtb_DA are sample IDs
rownames(mtb_DA)  # should look like "H001", "A004", etc.

# 2. Reorder metadata to match mtb_DA
idx <- match(rownames(mtb_DA), metadata$Sample)
metadata_aligned <- metadata[idx, ]

# Check alignment
stopifnot(all(metadata_aligned$Sample == rownames(mtb_DA)))
Group   <- factor(metadata_aligned$Study.Group)
Sex     <- factor(metadata_aligned$Gender)
Smoking <- factor(metadata_aligned$`Chem ID / Smoking history`)
AgeGroup <- factor(metadata_aligned$Age)
Race <- factor(metadata_aligned$Race)

tab_sex <- table(Group, Sex)
tab_sex
fisher.test(tab_sex)


tab_smoke <- table(Group, Smoking)
tab_smoke
fisher.test(tab_smoke)

tab_age <- table(Group,AgeGroup)
tab_age
fisher.test(tab_age)

tab_race <- table(Group,Race)
tab_race
fisher.test(tab_race)
```

## DEA of Metabolites Using LIMMA 

```{r}
library(limma)

## 1. Make sure mtb_DA orientation is correct
## limma expects rows = features, columns = samples.
## If your rows are samples, transpose first:
mtb_DA <- t(mtb_DA)

## 2. Group factor aligned to sample order
group <- factor(
  metadata_aligned$Study.Group[match(colnames(mtb_DA), metadata_aligned$Sample)],
  levels = c("Control", "Adenoma", "Carcinoma")  # adjust if needed
)
names(group) <- colnames(mtb_DA)

## 3. Design matrix
design <- model.matrix(~ -1 + group)
colnames(design)
# should be: "groupControl" "groupAdenoma" "groupCarcinoma"

table(group)   # check sample counts per group

## 4. Fit limma model
fit  <- lmFit(mtb_DA, design)
fit  <- eBayes(fit)

## 5. Correct contrasts (note the exact column names)
cont.matrix <- makeContrasts(
  Adenoma_vs_Control    = groupAdenoma   - groupControl,
  Carcinoma_vs_Control  = groupCarcinoma - groupControl,
  Carcinoma_vs_Adenoma  = groupCarcinoma - groupAdenoma,
  levels = design
)

fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, cont.matrix)
fit2 <- eBayes(fit2)

## 6. Extract tables

# Adenoma vs Control
tt_adenoma <- topTable(
  fit2,
  coef = "Adenoma_vs_Control",
  number = Inf,
  adjust.method = "BH"
)
tt_adenoma$FC          <- 2 ^ (tt_adenoma$logFC)
tt_adenoma$negLog10FDR <- -log10(tt_adenoma$adj.P.Val)

# Carcinoma vs Control
tt_carcinoma_control <- topTable(
  fit2,
  coef = "Carcinoma_vs_Control",
  number = Inf,
  adjust.method = "BH"
)
tt_carcinoma_control$FC          <- 2 ^ (tt_carcinoma_control$logFC)
tt_carcinoma_control$negLog10FDR <- -log10(tt_carcinoma_control$adj.P.Val)

# Carcinoma vs Adenoma
tt_carcinoma_adenoma <- topTable(
  fit2,
  coef = "Carcinoma_vs_Adenoma",
  number = Inf,
  adjust.method = "BH"
)
tt_carcinoma_adenoma$FC          <- 2 ^ (tt_carcinoma_adenoma$logFC)
tt_carcinoma_adenoma$negLog10FDR <- -log10(tt_carcinoma_adenoma$adj.P.Val)
```


```{r}
library(globaltest)

# samples x metabolites
X <- t(mtb_DA )  # rows = samples, cols = metabolites (your code already uses this)

stopifnot(all(rownames(X) == metadata_aligned$Sample))

meta <- metadata_aligned
meta$Study.Group <- factor(meta$Study.Group)

# subset to Control and Adenoma
sub_AC  <- meta$Study.Group %in% c("Control", "Adenoma")
X_AC    <- X[sub_AC, , drop = FALSE]
meta_AC <- droplevels(meta[sub_AC, , drop = FALSE])



# check levels
levels(meta_AC$Study.Group)

# Globaltest without covariates:
# response = Study.Group (factor), covariates = X_AC (metabolites)
gt_AC <- gt(meta_AC$Study.Group, X_AC)
summary(gt_AC)

# Globaltest **with** covariates (Age, Sex) uses the formula interface:
# null model: Study.Group ~ Age + Sex
# alternative: add the metabolite set (X_AC)
gt_AC_adj <- gt(Study.Group ~ Age + Gender, X_AC, data = meta_AC)
summary(gt_AC_adj)

```

## =============================================================================
## Metagenomics  data 
## =============================================================================


```{r}
# assume meg: rows = samples, cols = features (genes/metabolites)
dim(meg)

# filter features with total count > 10 (adjust threshold if needed)
meg <- meg[, colSums(meg) > 10]
dim(meg)
library(vegan)

alpha_shannon <- diversity(, index = "shannon")
alpha_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = names(alpha_shannon),
  Shannon = alpha_shannon,
  Group = metadata_aligned$Study.Group
)

ggplot(alpha_df, aes(Group, Shannon, fill = Group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "Shannon diversity", x = "", title = "Alpha diversity by group")
```

```{r}
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

X <- meg              # samples x taxa
meta <- metadata_aligned

stopifnot(all(rownames(X) == meta$Sample))

# Bray–Curtis distance (common for microbiome)
dist_bc <- vegdist(X, method = "bray")

# PCoA using base R cmdscale
pcoa_res <- cmdscale(dist_bc, eig = TRUE, k = 2)  # 2D solution

pcoa_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = rownames(X),
  PC1 = pcoa_res$points[, 1],
  PC2 = pcoa_res$points[, 2]
)

# merge with metadata
pcoa_df <- left_join(
  pcoa_df,
  meta,
  by = "Sample"
)

# percentage of variance explained
var_expl <- 100 * pcoa_res$eig[1:2] / sum(pcoa_res$eig[pcoa_res$eig > 0])

ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Study.Group)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.9) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PCoA1 (", round(var_expl[1], 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PCoA2 (", round(var_expl[2], 1), "%)"),
    color = "Group",
    title = "PCoA of microbiome profiles by group"
  )
```
